assign.outcome:
**One seam proposed, one refuted — and nothing under `core/` moved.** [Children that live in data](/framework/core/Page/doc/data-children/) is the whole deliverable: the problem in five sentences, the diff for each seam as fenced code, and the numbers.

**Seam 1 — `children` may be a function returning a promise. Proposed.** Core calls it once, memoises it, and awaits it inside `child()` and `load_all_children()`; whatever it answers with is declared then, in every form `children:` already takes. The prize is not the sugar — it is that the guard both callers had to copy (and both shipped the "Chaining cycle detected for promise" bug without, until 2026-09-05) stays above the await, in core, where a page cannot get it wrong.

**Seam 2 — a core `Page.redraw()`. Refuted, with three reasons from the code.** `content()` is where pages subscribe, so re-running it double-subscribes silently; `Router.mark()` holds the *view*, so a swapped view leaves the Router marking a detached element and the new one unmarked (`display: none`, nothing thrown); and a rebuilt view throws away the `regions` / `$pages` its children are standing in. All three data-backed pages already converge on the narrower pattern that works — own a box, `empty()` it, refill, re-run `mark_links()`.

**The numbers.** ~22 lines added to `Page.class.js` (8 code). 79 deleted from the two callers, 16 written back — **net 63 fewer**. **18 urls** would run it today. Real cost: two new names on `Page` (`child_source`, `source_children()`), which is what the owner is being asked to approve.

![](data-children-1280.png)

**Also added:** one **proposed** line in [`core/Page/readme.md`](/framework/core/Page/) "More", and entry 5 under [`doc/decisions.md`](/framework/core/Page/doc/decisions/) "## Proposed" — clicked through in-app, it lands on the new page with no console errors.

**Two findings on the way past, not fixed (the fence forbids `/imagine/`):** `imagine/importance/page.js` overrides `activate()` in 5 lines to redraw on every visit, when core already calls `activated?.()` — one line would do. And `cms/json`'s `redraw()` never re-runs `mark_links()`, which `doc/declaring.md` already names as a bug class.

**Deliberately left:** the diff is not implemented and was checked by reading, as briefed. The doc is reached by the `.md` fallback rather than `page.js`'s `notes:` list, so it costs the one documented probe 404 on `data-children/page.js`; adding it to `notes:` is a one-word edit outside this task's fence.
